summary.text: Vince Fong is the Republican incumbent for California's 20th District, a Bakersfield native who worked for Reps. Bill Thomas and Kevin McCarthy before serving in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2024. He won a May 2024 special election to succeed McCarthy and a full term that November, and advanced from the June 2026 primary.

paragraphs.text: Fong was born in Bakersfield and says he has always called the region home. He earned a bachelor's degree from UCLA in 2001 and a master's degree from Princeton University in 2003.

He began his career in public policy with Rep. Bill Thomas, then chair of the House Ways and Means Committee, working on international trade policy. After returning to Kern County, he spent nearly a decade as district director to Kevin McCarthy, then House Majority Leader. He also helped organize a Valley Fever Symposium to bring national attention to the disease.

Fong was elected to the California State Assembly in 2016 and served until 2024, representing District 32 after 2022. His official biography says he worked in Sacramento on energy, transportation, infrastructure and supply chains.

After McCarthy resigned from Congress, Fong ran in the special election for the 20th District. He defeated fellow Republican Mike Boudreaux in the May 21, 2024 runoff, 60.6 percent to 39.4 percent, and won a full term in November 2024 with 65.1 percent against Boudreaux.

In Congress he serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure, Science, Space, and Technology, and Homeland Security committees, and he belongs to the Republican Study Committee, Western Caucus and Congressional Valley Fever Task Force, among other caucuses.
Fong advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary with 68.2 percent of the vote. He is a lifelong Kern County resident and lives in Bakersfield with his wife, Amanda.
